clue.text: Tropical bird giving many a raucous cry

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
a caw is the harsh call of a crow

explanation.surface: A parrot in the jungle squawks loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large brightly coloured parrot of Central and South American rainforests.

clue.text: Saunter round northern capital, obtaining picture

indicators.note: the strolling word goes round the northern letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to mooch is to wander or saunter aimlessly
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Someone strolls about a northern capital city and comes away with a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A monochrome is a painting or photograph done in shades of a single colour.

clue.text: Salad ingredient in the Dodecanese?

definitions.meaning: ..., also spelt Kos, is one of the Greek Dodecanese islands

explanation.definitionFit: Cos lettuce is named after the Greek island of Cos, so both senses share one word.

clue.text: Fitness husband initially sacrificed for wife's riches

indicators.note: the first letter, the husband's H at the start, is given up in favour of the wife's letter

parts.note: fitness here means good health
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A husband gives up his fitness so his wife can be rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' places the swap at the very start: the leading H of the fitness word becomes W.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth is a stock of money and possessions, a synonym for riches.

clue.text: Condition imposed in key match

indicators.note: the condition is set into the middle of the key word

parts.note: seminal means key or highly influential
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A stipulation is written into an important football fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A semifinal is a match whose winner goes through to the final.

clue.text: US soldiers upset woman keeping home for Miss Italy

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the soldiers' letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

indicators.note: the woman's name holds the home word inside it

parts.note: Nora is a woman's name
in means at home

explanation.surface: American troops trouble a woman who keeps house, in the cause of an Italian beauty queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Signorina is the Italian title for an unmarried woman, the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: Designs by all these? Certainly

definitions.meaning: the phrase 'by all ...' meaning certainly, completed with this word

explanation.definitionFit: Means is a verb for intends or designs, and 'by all means' is an emphatic certainly.

clue.text: Old soldier's stuffiness depresses lover

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on top of the other presses it down, so the stuffy word comes first

parts.note: a fug is a stuffy, smoky atmosphere
leman is an old word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: An old soldier's musty air weighs on his sweetheart's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after soldier stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugleman was a well-drilled soldier placed in front of a company as a model for the others.

clue.text: Myopic journalist supports listeners kept in dark

indicators.note: in a down clue the journalist sits underneath, holding the rest up
the listeners are held inside the dark word

parts.note: night is darkness
ears are what we listen with
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A short-sighted reporter backs eavesdroppers who are left uninformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopic and near-sighted both describe seeing close objects clearly but distant ones blurred.

clue.text: Oral part of course in Finno-Ugric language?

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the course word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a racecourse

explanation.surface: A spoken section of a class in a Uralic language.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapp is a name for the Sami language of northern Scandinavia, a Finno-Ugric tongue.

clue.text: Lost again in the wild, longing for home

indicators.note: running wild, the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Lost once more in the wilderness, someone yearns to go home.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia originally meant homesickness, a painful longing to return home.

clue.text: Understanding doctor's literally 17?

indicators.note: the answer to 17 is to be read letter by letter as an instruction

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
17-down split into its letters reads RAS PUT IN

explanation.surface: Is a doctor's comprehension really just the Russian mystic?
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' asks us to read the 17-down answer as a sentence: split it after its third letter and it becomes an instruction to put something in.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasp of a subject is a firm understanding of it.

clue.text: Polite manner one uses freely in trying situations

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the trying word

parts.note: courts are where cases are tried

indicators.note: used freely, the letters are rearranged at will

explanation.surface: Good manners are what one deploys generously when things get tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying situations' suggests hardship, but it means places where cases are tried; 'freely' makes EOUSNES from the scrambled pair of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Courteousness is politeness or good manners in behaviour.

clue.text: Indifferent firm taken in by university man

indicators.note: the firm is enclosed by the university man's letters

parts.note: Ned is a man's name
a concern is a business or firm

explanation.surface: An apathetic company is swindled by a man from a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconcerned means not worried or caring, which is to be indifferent.

clue.text: One seeks information about chief prophet externally

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the prophet lies on the outside, around the chief word

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
arch means chief, as in arch-enemy

explanation.surface: Someone digs for facts about a leading visionary from the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A researcher investigates a subject to discover information about it.

clue.text: Lively copper leaving church office

indicators.note: the copper departs from the church office word, which is left without it

parts.note: a curacy is the office of a curate
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An energetic policeman quits his job in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy writing or style is lively and spirited, often slightly risque.

clue.text: Conservative aspect of a good number of degrees?

parts.note: the right is the conservative wing of politics
an angle is a point of view or aspect

explanation.surface: A Tory viewpoint held by many graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degrees' suggests university qualifications, but these are degrees of angle: ninety of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A right angle measures ninety degrees, a fair number of them, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Such music, written down, getting someone's goat, perhaps

parts.note: a down is a rolling hill, as in the South Downs
a billy is a male goat, also a man's name

explanation.surface: Country music, once transcribed, irritates somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting someone's goat' looks like the idiom for annoying a person, but it is the billy goat; 'written' tells us the hill word is set down above it in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Hillbilly music is old-time country music from the rural American South.

clue.text: Peasant monk puts out in bad weather

indicators.note: the mixed letters sit inside the weather word

parts.note: rain is bad weather

indicators.note: put out of order, the letters rearrange

explanation.surface: A peasant monk puts things outside during a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts out' reads as setting things outdoors, but 'out' is the anagram signal, giving SPUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasputin was the Siberian peasant mystic and self-styled holy man at the Russian court.

clue.text: Male friend gripping macaw today in obsessive way

indicators.note: the male and friend words hold the macaw reference between them

parts.note: man means a male person
an ally is a friend
in today's puzzle the macaw is the answer at 1 across, abbreviated 1ac

explanation.surface: A man's pal clutches a parrot this very day, quite obsessively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'macaw today' means where macaw appears today: 1-across, written 1AC and read as IAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Maniacally means in a frenzied, obsessed manner, like a maniac.

clue.text: Council finally abandons design, producing eyesore

indicators.note: the letter leaves the design word behind, taken out of it

parts.note: a style is a design or fashion

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of council

explanation.surface: The council gives up on a scheme, leaving an ugly building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyesore' looks like a blot on the landscape, but it is literally a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore eye.

clue.text: Appropriate to issue current article when in charge

indicators.note: the current and article letters are placed inside the charge word

parts.note: to fill is to charge or load, as with a glass
I is the symbol for electric current
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something fitting to hand out an up-to-date item while in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means children, not something handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Filial describes what is due from a son or daughter, issue being a word for offspring.

clue.text: Self-seeking tycoon who erected theatre in Hackney?

definitions.meaning: a person who seeks to grow their own power and organisation
the Hackney Empire is a famous London music-hall theatre, so its builder

explanation.definitionFit: An empire builder is someone who amasses power for themselves, and literally whoever built the Hackney Empire.

clue.text: Game preceding business administrator's dance

indicators.note: the game comes before the administrator in the answer

parts.note: RU is rugby union
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A match comes before a manager's ballroom number.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Single pharmacist's naughty children

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MPS stands for Member of the Pharmaceutical Society, a pharmacist

explanation.surface: A lone chemist's badly behaved kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Imps are mischievous little creatures, a term for naughty children.

clue.text: Paid on being engaged, he painted Rouen Cathedral

indicators.note: the word on is engaged, held within the payment word

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it, so met is paid

explanation.surface: Paid once hired, an artist painted a French cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet painted a famous series of views of Rouen Cathedral in the 1890s.

clue.text: May perhaps evil one intrude a very tiny bit?

indicators.note: the evil and one letters push into the middle of the month word

parts.note: May is an example of a month
ill can mean evil, as in ill deeds
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Might a wicked person barge in just a little?
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the verb of permission, but it is the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A millionth is one part in a million, a minute fraction.

clue.text: Darling dog wanting a type of bread

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter a is dropped

parts.note: Nana is the Darling family's dog in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A beloved hound without a particular loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' looks like an endearment, but it is the family name in J M Barrie's Peter Pan, whose nursemaid is the dog Nana.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan or nan is a leavened flatbread from South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Somehow, years tend to make us inactive

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are reordered in some way

explanation.surface: The passing years tend to slow us down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary means sitting a lot and taking little exercise, so inactive.

clue.text: Vessel for cosmetic

definitions.meaning: make-up drawn along the eye or lip edge

explanation.definitionFit: A liner is both a large passenger ship and an eyeliner or lip liner pencil.
